issues.description: download_and_untar.sh warns when unzip is missing but does not exit, then fails cryptically later.
issues.detail: The `command -v unzip` check echoes a message and falls through; later extraction calls then die noisily mid-run. Precondition checks must fail fast at the boundary. Add `exit 1` after the warning so the script aborts cleanly when the required tool is absent.

issues.description: Three near-identical TAL_ASR-{1,2,3} extraction blocks should be one loop over a small table.
issues.detail: Each archive gets a copy-pasted block differing only in zip name and target subdir. That regularity is data, not control flow. Replace with a small table (zip, subdir, label) and a loop. Cuts ~30 lines, removes drift risk, and makes adding a fourth archive trivial.

issues.description: run.sh sets use_lm=false but README advertises LM-decoded results — recipe and docs disagree.
issues.detail: The recipe disables the LM yet README reports `decode_asr_branchformer_lm_...` rows as reproducible. A user running run.sh as-is cannot reproduce those numbers. Either default `use_lm=true` to match the documented results or drop the LM args and document the override required.

issues.description: download_and_untar.sh never downloads and usage branch falls through without exit.
issues.detail: Despite its name, the script only extracts; archives missing produce a message and success exit. The arg-count usage branch also cats help then continues with unset $1, producing a confusing realpath error. Either rename to extract.sh and honor the new contract, or download when archives are absent; in either case, exit non-zero on bad args.

issues.description: README links to ./conf/train/train_asr_branchformer_e24_amp.yaml but the file lives at ./conf/.
issues.detail: The README path has a spurious `train/` segment; the config is at `./conf/train_asr_branchformer_e24_amp.yaml`. Broken link on GitHub. Fix the path so readers can find the config.

issues.description: Transcript normalization is an opaque chain of seds; rules should be data, not pipeline plumbing.
issues.detail: Six piped seds applying single-character substitutions could be one `sed -e ... -e ...` or a `tr -d` plus a trailing-space sed. Better yet, extract the substitution table into a named mapping so adding a punctuation rule touches data, not shell plumbing.

synthesis.summary: The panel agrees this is a standard ESPnet recipe contribution whose template-conforming parts are fine, but whose two real shell drivers (local/data.sh and local/download_and_untar.sh) have fail-soft branches that should fail hard and copy-pasted blocks that should be small table-driven loops. The most material defects are contract mismatches: download_and_untar.sh doesn't exit when unzip is missing and doesn't actually download, and run.sh disables the LM that README claims as a reproducible result. Documentation drift (broken README config path) and incidental complexity in the sed-chain normalization round out the cleanup list. None of the issues are algorithmically broken; they are spec/shape problems that should be reconciled before merge.
